issues.description: Tests patched with placeholder zero-amount Addition to mask a behavior change in the empty-additions path
issues.detail: Both tests replaced additions=[] with Addition(amount=0, puzzle_hash=zeros) to satisfy the new len(additions) >= 1 invariant in CreateSignedTransaction.__post_init__. This silently changes which code path is exercised and hides a breaking change for real callers that passed empty lists. Add a regression test for the empty-list path or document the break.

issues.description: Per-addition MAX_COIN_AMOUNT bounds check silently removed from cat_spend
issues.detail: Old cat_spend raised ValueError when any addition exceeded MAX_COIN_AMOUNT. The new code forwards request.additions to create_signed_transaction without showing equivalent enforcement. Either prove the downstream path enforces the same bound or restore the explicit check. Silently dropping bounds validation in a deduplication patch is exactly how subtle regressions ship.

issues.description: CreateSignedTransaction has become a god-struct complecting XCH, CAT, and clawback concerns
issues.detail: The request type now carries extra_delta, tail_reveal, tail_solution (CAT-only) plus puzzle_decorator (XCH-only, with a comment admitting the type is a hack) alongside generic additions, gated only by None checks. The all-or-none invariant on the CAT triple is enforced lazily at the property accessor rather than at construction. Define proper variants or enforce invariants in __post_init__.

issues.description: In-process JSON round-trip via json_serialize_for_transport is gratuitous
issues.detail: Both new handlers build a typed CreateSignedTransaction, serialize to JSON, then create_signed_transaction re-parses it — same process, same memory. This complects the value layer with the wire format and costs cycles on every internal call. Either have create_signed_transaction accept the typed object, or factor a shared inner function both call.

issues.description: get_wallet called purely for its raising side effect with a cryptic comment
issues.detail: Both handlers call self.service.wallet_state_manager.get_wallet(...) and discard the result, annotated only with '# opportunity to raise'. This complects identity resolution with input validation and runs the lookup twice on every call. Extract a named _assert_wallet_type(id, required_type) helper or let create_signed_transaction perform the check once.

issues.description: cat_discrepancy_validation invariant is subtle and unstated, requiring type: ignore suppressions
issues.detail: The helper's all-None-or-none-None precondition is not expressed in the types, forcing three type: ignore comments and relying on a subtle 'None in {set}' idiom. Lift the precondition into a small frozen CatDiscrepancy dataclass with a from_optionals classmethod returning Optional[CatDiscrepancy], so coercions live with the value and the invariant is named.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this PR is labeled as deduplication but is really centralization that hides behavior changes. Two P0 issues stand out: tests were patched with sentinel zero-amount Additions to slip past a new len>=1 invariant (masking a breaking change for empty-list callers), and the per-addition MAX_COIN_AMOUNT bounds check appears to have been silently dropped from cat_spend. Structurally, CreateSignedTransaction has become a god-request braiding XCH, CAT, and clawback concerns with lazy invariant checks, in-process calls pay gratuitous JSON round-trip cost, and get_wallet is used as a discarded validation side effect. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — restore the bounds check, prove the empty-additions semantics, enforce invariants at construction, and split the patch.
